_comment: Committed performance baseline for the fold_db criterion benches.
This is the SOURCE OF TRUTH the scheduled/label-gated `bench` CI job
(.github/workflows/bench.yml) compares fresh bench runs against — it
replaces the hand-typed numbers that used to live (and go stale) in the
bench doc comments. See README.md in this directory.
Captured from origin/main @ be19526be on a shared machine with
FOLD_DISABLE_NATIVE_INDEX=1 (the env the benches set themselves), 2026-06-21.
Every `baseline_ns` is the criterion MEDIAN point-estimate, in nanoseconds.
The guard (scripts/lints/bench-compare.py) reads each fresh run's
target/criterion/<group>/<id>/new/estimates.json and fails the case when
fresh_median_ns > baseline_ns * regression_factor.
regression_factor defaults to 2.0 (the card's '>2x regression' bar);
the FLAT cases (point lookups, which must NOT scale with cardinality) are
guarded tighter at 1.6x so an O(field) regression like the 2026-06-20 wedge
trips the guard well before it 2x's. Absolute numbers are runner-dependent;
treat these as RELATIVE regression ceilings, not SLAs.
Cases with fast_guard_optional=true are still part of full local benchmark
runs, but may be absent from the scheduled FOLD_BENCH_FAST_GUARD=1 CI pass
when their setup cost would starve later guard suites.
Updating: when a deliberate perf change moves a curve, re-run the benches on
a quiet machine (see README) and edit the affected baseline_ns here in the
same PR, with the reason in the commit message.

captured._schema_scan_note: schema_scan + schema_scan_indexed re-captured 2026-07-17 after schemaidx markers moved out of the main atom namespace and into the local-only schema_index namespace. schema_scan remains result-sized and schema_scan_indexed remains flat across corpus size. The fixed-result schema_scan_indexed cases were rechecked on the loaded scheduled-routine host on 2026-07-18: medians were ~4.36ms/6.66ms/5.09ms/4.10ms for 1K/10K/50K/100K, so the flat baseline is rounded to 7ms with the same 1.6x guard. A real fallback to the old full scan remains far above this ceiling.

captured._batch_store_note: batch_store cases captured 2026-07-15 on a loaded shared host after the bench switched to fresh DBs per measured iteration so corpus growth cannot distort later samples. The one-atom case was rechecked on the loaded scheduled-routine host on 2026-07-19 at ~25.7ms median and rounded to 30ms; larger cases remain from the 2026-07-15 capture (~11.86ms/3.22ms/82.01ms for 10/100/1000 atoms). Baselines are relative ceilings only.
captured._storage_breakdown_note: storage_breakdown cases added 2026-07-25 to make per-schema logical storage metering attribution visible in the db-perf guard. The current implementation scans canonical atom rows and filters to the requested schema, so the curve is expected to be linear in total corpus with a fixed 500-atom target result. Initial baselines are conservative shared-runner ceilings; if storage_breakdown moves to schema-index enumeration, re-capture and flatten these cases.
captured._hash_key_lookup_note: query_path_bench HashKey lookup cases re-captured 2026-07-18 from origin/main @ 7aa2c8589 on the scheduled routine host after confirming the current-head mhk fast path already bypasses transient molecule hydration. The remaining cardinality growth is the sled atom-body point-get curve: indexed_point_lookup medians were ~27.6us/69.9us/132.7us/214.1us for 1k/10k/50k/100k. Baselines keep the 1.6x guard to catch a return to field materialization while acknowledging that one marker get plus one atom-body get is not perfectly flat on this store.
captured._atom_refcount_tip_write_note: atom_refcount_tip_write_vs_catalog_refs captured 2026-09-28 on the shared Apple Silicon host after the tip path moved from a catalog-edge partition scan to one exact durable counter read per molecule. Fast-guard medians were ~103ms/144ms/190ms for 0/16/64 catalog aliases. Baselines round upward because full mutation durability dominates and shared-host noise is large; the curve now records this added cost and guards against a return to an edge scan.
